assets.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: photoreal interior concept view for the existing Dusk apartment, exactly ONE native 1536x1024 landscape image.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET and sole authority for camera, lens, room perimeter, geometry, openings and all fixed fixtures. Edit this photograph in place. The original left foreground door leaf/handle, left-wall AC, corner bay window, each window sill, ceiling and ceiling light, right-side window and city view must remain in their exact positions and sizes. Keep the exact same camera height, camera position, perspective, focal length, crop and 3:2 aspect ratio.

Primary request: ACTUALLY REVERSE THE BED POSITION as a furniture-only conceptual swap. Remove the bed/headboard from the right wall. Relocate its fine cognac leather headboard to the LEFT SOLID WALL underneath the AC and where the console is now, with the pillows against that left headboard; the foot of the bed now points toward the ORIGINAL RIGHT-SIDE HEADBOARD WALL. The pillows and headboard must be visibly on the LEFT of the finished image, and the bed foot must be toward the RIGHT, the opposite of the source. Remove the left console. Move the original tall walnut wardrobe from the left to the solid right wall zone formerly behind the bed, with slender vertical walnut doors and subtle dark handles. Make this swap unmistakable, not a new bedding color on the existing bed placement. Keep a believable passage past the bed and wardrobe. If the locked original camera cannot see the entire new headboard, allow it to be naturally cropped rather than changing camera or expanding the room.
Keep the bay glazing at the back completely unobstructed; preserve its corner joint and sill. Do not place wardrobe over either window. Preserve the original near-left entry door and its handle, distinguishing that door from the wardrobe being relocated. Do not add any new doors, openings or floor area.
Style: high quality believable architectural photograph, same Dusk luxe warm walnut aesthetic, fine cognac leather bed, ivory textured bedding, folded cocoa throw, quiet stone-beige walls, warm walnut floor and subtle brass lighting details, understated and realistic.
Lighting: neutral natural daytime with soft warm daylight, small existing practical lamps may glow gently. Keep city light realistic, no deep dusk or orange cast.
Avoid: changed camera, enlarged room, remodeled architecture, new openings, shifted window or sill or AC, a mirrored entire room, same bed location as source, generic layout diagram, UI, captions, labels, branding, watermark, people, cinematic blur. Output only the single finished photographic image.

observations: Bed orientation visibly reversed: cognac headboard/pillows at left, foot toward right; new tall walnut wardrobe on original right headboard wall.
Original corner bay, separate right window, AC, ceiling light and near-left door handle are visually retained; no material camera or room-perimeter shift observed.
The left foreground walnut panel with long dark handle remains, so relocation of the entire original left wardrobe is not conclusively depicted; could read as remaining cabinetry beside entry.
Right-wall wardrobe is broad and floor-to-ceiling; its practical depth, door clearance and walking clearance are illustrative and unmeasured.
Original bedroom art above right headboard is removed behind new wardrobe; left framed art remains.

assets.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: photoreal conceptual interior edit for the existing Dusk apartment balcony, exactly ONE native 1536x1024 landscape image.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET. Preserve EXACTLY the original camera height, camera position, lens, perspective, composition, 3:2 crop and fixed balcony outline. Keep the side jambs, upper beam, exterior slab edge, original glazed opening WIDTH, right walnut wall, curtains, near sliding door frame and floor track, and stone floor plane at their original positions. Keep the balcony enclosed.

Primary request: visualize the concept of FLOOR-TO-CEILING GLAZING INSIDE THE EXISTING OPENING WIDTH. Replace ONLY the opaque lower exterior infill beneath the original outside window by transparent glass in this conceptual image, extending glass visually down to the interior floor/slab edge. This is an architectural concept image, not a statement of buildability. Preserve all side jambs and top beam, never make the opening wider or taller. Keep a slim, credible non-climbable inner guard/barrier detail: simple clear inner glass panel with minimal slim vertical supports and a single slim top rail, no climbable horizontal ladders. Maintain believable sealed glazing and subtle glass reflections and frame joints. Keep the high-floor Shanghai residential skyline at a believable distance, naturally extending the view downward through the new lower glass.
Remove the bulky long central bench and small freestanding bronze table to reveal ample clear stone floor. Put a very slim wall-mounted folding WALNUT TEA LEDGE on the RIGHT wall, shown folded down horizontally, open for use, supported by compact discreet folding brackets. A small ceramic teacup may sit on it. Add ONE light movable cognac leather/timber chair tucked at the right side, leaving the center free. Keep a small warm task lamp at right, fine stone floor and Dusk walnut detailing. Remove the oversized potted tree if necessary to keep the right tea ledge and chair usable and visible.
Lighting: neutral natural daytime, realistic soft Shanghai daylight and subtle warm task light. Photoreal architectural quality with fine materials, realistic perspective and texture.
Avoid: open exterior deck, removed top beam or side jamb, larger opening, larger balcony, moved camera, dramatic fisheye, floor extended past slab edge, unguarded edge, climbable horizontal rail ladder, big central bench, extra chairs, heavy table, garden fantasy, UI, app interface, caption, label, watermark, branding or people. Do not add any written safety, structural or installation claim inside the image. Output only one finished photographic image.
